inputFacts.title: Detroit woman sexually exploited, trafficked missing 16-year-old girl, feds say
inputFacts.summary: Federal authorities allege a Detroit woman sexually exploited and trafficked a missing 16-year-old girl. Investigators identified the suspect, Jasmina Vukojevic, through a tattooed hand image and selfie-style photos on her phone. She is scheduled to appear in federal court on Oct. 27 for a status conference and has prior convictions for weapons and drug charges in Wayne and Macomb counties.

inputFacts.title: SACUA discusses Statement of Student Rights and Responsibilities amendments, faculty housing
inputFacts.summary: The University of Michigan’s Senate Advisory Committee on University Affairs met to discuss amending the Statement of Student Rights and Responsibilities and addressing faculty housing challenges amid Ann Arbor’s housing affordability crisis. SACUA Chair Kentaro Toyama highlighted enrollment demographic shifts and plans to collaborate with Central Student Government following a sexual assault case at Cornell University. The committee approved 22 of 28 proposed amendments to student rights policies and plans to revisit faculty housing recommendations after gathering more data on salaries and housing costs.

inputFacts.title: Why mailing a ballot close to Election Day may get it rejected for a late postmark
inputFacts.summary: USPS's 'Regional Transportation Optimization' plan, implemented since April 2025, has reduced mail pick-ups and altered postmark procedures, risking late postmarks for ballots. USPS is taking 'extraordinary measures' to manually postmark ballots starting Oct. 26, but analysts warn of potential ballot rejections due to unclear implementation and staffing challenges.

inputFacts.title: Michigan voters can request absentee ballots for November election
inputFacts.summary: Voters in Michigan can spoil already submitted absentee ballots by submitting a written request to their local clerk's office. Requests must be signed and specify whether a new ballot should be mailed or picked up in person. The deadline for requests is 5 p.m. on October 23 for the November election. Voters who cast ballots at early voting sites or polling locations cannot spoil their ballots.

inputFacts.title: Benson and James clash over financial integrity, tax plans in final debate
inputFacts.summary: Michigan gubernatorial candidates Jocelyn Benson and John James debated in Detroit on October 24, 2026, focusing on tax policies, data center transparency, and economic growth. Benson emphasized affordability and accountability while James highlighted energy cost reduction and experience. Both candidates attacked each other's financial ties to data centers and policy records.

inputFacts.title: Dingell, Balint and Rheingans talk healthcare, social security at Ann Arbor town hall
inputFacts.summary: Ann Arbor community members gathered at Detroit Street Filling Station for a town hall organized by Abdul El-Sayed’s U.S. Senate campaign. U.S. Rep. Debbie Dingell, U.S. Rep. Becca Balint, and state Rep. Carrie Rheingans discussed threats to Social Security and Medicare from Trump-era budget cuts, emphasizing the need for Medicare for All and voter engagement. Panelists highlighted impacts on small businesses and healthcare accessibility.

inputFacts.title: Republicans put spotlight on Abdul El-Sayed. He welcomes the fight
inputFacts.summary: Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic U.S. Senate candidate in Michigan, faces intense Republican attacks portraying him as a radical, while embracing a confrontational campaign style. The race, one of the nation's most consequential, features a Republican spending advantage and national stakes, with figures like Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Barack Obama planning to campaign for El-Sayed. His approach has divided Democrats but energized progressive supporters.

inputFacts.title: Saroki’s is giving away free pizza and chicken across Michigan
inputFacts.summary: Saroki’s Crispy Chicken & Pizza is offering free food at all 22 Michigan locations on October 24 as a thank-you to customers. From 11 a.m.-5 p.m., customers can receive one pizza slice, one chicken tender, and a side of sauce while supplies last. Founder Todd Saroki stated the event aims to show appreciation for community support over 15 years.

inputFacts.title: Grammy Award-winning singer Samara Joy performs at Hill Auditorium
inputFacts.summary: Grammy Award-winning jazz singer Samara Joy performed at the University of Michigan’s Hill Auditorium as part of her 2026 world tour promoting her upcoming EP. The concert, organized by the University Musical Society, featured songs from her albums and a preview of her new EP, with Joy emphasizing the preparation and chemistry of her septet. Attendees praised the emotional and enlightening experience of witnessing her live performance.

inputFacts.title: Absentee Ballots Going Out in Michigan: What to Know
inputFacts.summary: Michigan requires local communities to offer at least nine days of early in-person voting, a change approved by voters in 2022. Early voting will start on Oct. 24 in most areas, or earlier in some locations where clerks allow additional days.
